# Effects

Every effect and generator, from its descriptor: platform effects first, then the shipped shader plugins. Write effects/<name>.sksl beside comp.json: header comments `// @effect name`, `// @kind effect|generator`, `// @summary ...`, `// @param name float|vec2|color default [min max] -- doc`, `// @param name choice default a,b,c -- doc` (written as a name), `// @input name layer` (another layer's picture, named by id in the use), `// @input name history=N [depth=D]` (the effect's own output N frames ago), `// @pass name [scale=S]` (several passes, each sees the earlier ones by name), `// @space display|linear` (the encoding the shader computes in; see the colour key), `// @example {json}`, then `half4 main(float2 xy)`. You get `image` (effects), `resolution`, `time` and a library (hash21, vnoise, fbm, worley, rot2, luma, hsv2rgb, straight, premul). Try it with `comp fx test <name> --out sheet.png`; then use it like any effect: {"effect": "name", "param": value}.

## Composite options (every effect)

Every effect, built-in or plugin, takes an optional `composite`: the original picture stays visible and the effect's result is laid over it, only inside a mask, with a blend mode and an amount. Without it the result replaces the input.

* `blend`: any layer blend mode (default normal)
* `mask`: none (default) | alpha | {kind: luma, lo, hi, softness, invert} | {kind: edges, strength, width} | {kind: layer, layer: id, channel: luma|alpha, invert}
* `mix`: 0..1, animatable (default 1): how much of the laid-over result shows

```json
{
  "composite": {
    "blend": "screen",
    "mask": {
      "kind": "luma",
      "lo": 0.5,
      "softness": 0.2
    },
    "mix": 0.8
  },
  "effect": "halftone",
  "size": 12
}
```

## Effect space (`effect_space`, a composition key)

Where a layer's effects and masks run. "screen" (the default) paints every layer at the size of the frame with its transform applied and then runs its effects on that picture, so a 10 px blur is 10 screen pixels at any layer scale and content outside the frame never reaches an effect. "layer" is After Effects' order: the layer's own pixels first (the buffer grows by what its effects spread: blur, glow, drop shadow and the other effects that declare bounds), then its masks and effects, then its position, scale and rotation. A blur doubles with the layer's scale, a directional blur turns with it, and a bright shape half outside the frame still blurs into it. Layers without effects or masks, adjustment layers and `look` are unchanged. Effects that read the picture behind the layer (`backdrop`), another layer or the layer's own past (plugin layer and history inputs) and a mesh with effects have no meaning before the transform: `check` refuses them in a layer-space composition, naming the effect. A composition's own `effect_space` overrides the root's. A shader plugin declares how far it spreads with `// @bounds none | expand=<expr> | expand_x=<expr> expand_y=<expr>`; the `fx-needs-bounds` lint warns about a plugin that does not say.

```json
{
  "bg": "#10141f",
  "dur": 3,
  "effect_space": "layer",
  "fps": 30,
  "height": 720,
  "layers": [
    {
      "align": "center",
      "color": "#ffffff",
      "fx": [
        {
          "effect": "blur",
          "radius": 12
        }
      ],
      "pos": [
        640,
        360
      ],
      "scale": {
        "dur": 2.5,
        "ease": "sine.inOut",
        "from": 1,
        "to": 1.6
      },
      "size": 120,
      "text": "Soft focus",
      "type": "text",
      "weight": 800
    }
  ],
  "width": 1280
}
```

## Colour (`color`, a composition key)

What the numbers of a composition's pictures mean. Left out, nothing changes: every picture, colour and effect works on display-encoded sRGB numbers as it always did, and the render is byte-for-byte what it was. With `linear_light`, pictures are kept as light: blends, blurs, glows, gradients and resampling are computed on light, so 50% white over black is the mid-grey a lamp at half power gives (level 188 on screen, not 128), a blur across a black/white edge is half as bright as the pair on average (188, not 128), and an additive blend adds light. Colour literals, gradients, images and video are converted into the working profile as they are drawn, and the finished frame is converted to the output profile when it leaves, with alpha kept as coverage throughout (it is never encoded). Effects that move or spread light (blur, glow, shadow, exposure, the warps) run in light; effects written against what the eye sees (brightness, contrast, hue, tint, grain, grade) always run on display numbers, converted in and out around them, so their sliders feel the same in either mode. A shader plugin says which it wants with `// @space display|linear`. A nested composition takes the root's values field by field unless it says its own; `space` is the finished frame's profile, so only the root has it. The encoder tags the file with the output profile, so a player shows the colours the film was made with. `dither` changes how the finished frame is rounded to 8 bits and nothing else: with `ordered` or `blue_noise` a threshold pattern is added before the floor, on the numbers the file will hold (after the output conversion), so a smooth dark gradient shows no bands; the error is zero-mean and at most one level, the pattern is static, and the render is deterministic. A flat colour can move one level at a few pixels (half-float cannot hold every level exactly). It cannot outlast the codec: hardware H.264 and any 4:2:0 or lossy encode re-quantise the frames, so a 10-bit export is the real cure for banding in a delivered file.

* `depth`: Numeric depth of every picture: `half` (half-float, the only one, and what the engine always used).
* `dither`: Root only. How the finished frame is rounded to 8 bits: `none` or `ordered` or `blue_noise` (default none, which rounds to nearest and changes nothing).
* `linear_light`: true keeps pictures in linear light (default false: display-encoded numbers).
* `space`: Root only. The gamut the finished frame is encoded in, with the sRGB curve, and the file is tagged with: `srgb` or `display_p3` (default srgb).
* `working_profile`: The gamut pictures are kept in: `srgb` or `display_p3` (default srgb). Images with an embedded profile and video tagged with their primaries keep their colours when it is wider than the file's.

```json
{
  "bg": "#000000",
  "color": {
    "linear_light": true
  },
  "dur": 2,
  "fps": 30,
  "height": 720,
  "layers": [
    {
      "color": "#ffffff",
      "pos": [
        320,
        360
      ],
      "size": [
        640,
        720
      ],
      "type": "solid"
    },
    {
      "color": "#ffffff",
      "fx": [
        {
          "effect": "blur",
          "radius": 24
        }
      ],
      "opacity": 0.5,
      "size": [
        1280,
        720
      ],
      "type": "solid"
    }
  ],
  "width": 1280
}
```

## `blur`

Gaussian blur. (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | float | 8.0 | 0 or more | Gaussian sigma in pixels (After Effects' Blurriness is twice this). |
| `quality` | choice | legacy | legacy, exact | `legacy` is the blur films were first made with, kept so they render as they did (above a sigma of 4 a small source gains or loses up to a quarter of its light); `exact` is the kernel blur: the sigma asked for, no light lost, a reach of 4 sigma. |
| `dimensions` | choice | both | both, horizontal, vertical | Which way it blurs. |
| `edge` | choice | transparent | transparent, repeat | `transparent` lets light leave the picture's edge; `repeat` continues the edge pixels outward, and the layer does not grow. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by its reach (blur radius, distance, offset)
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "effect": "blur",
  "radius": 8
}
```

## `box_blur`

Box blur: the mean of a square, repeated for a softer, rounder fall-off. (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | float | 5.0 | 0 or more | Pixels each side of a pixel it averages; a fraction weights the outermost pixel. |
| `iterations` | float | 1.0 | 1 to 16 | Times the box is repeated; 3 or more is close to a Gaussian. |
| `dimensions` | choice | both | both, horizontal, vertical | Which way it blurs. |
| `edge` | choice | transparent | transparent, repeat | `transparent` lets light leave the picture's edge; `repeat` continues the edge pixels outward, and the layer does not grow. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by its reach (blur radius, distance, offset)
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "effect": "box_blur",
  "iterations": 3,
  "radius": 6
}
```

## `lens_blur`

Lens blur: every pixel becomes the lens's opening, a disc or a polygon. (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | float | 10.0 | 0 to 31.5 | Pixels from the centre of the opening to its farthest part. |
| `blades` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 16 | Sides of the opening: 0 for a disc, or 3 to 16. |
| `rotation` | float | 0.0 |  | Degrees the polygon is turned. |
| `roundness` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 1 | 0 keeps the polygon's straight sides, 1 rounds it to a disc. |
| `edge` | choice | transparent | transparent, repeat | `transparent` lets light leave the picture's edge; `repeat` continues the edge pixels outward, and the layer does not grow. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by its reach (blur radius, distance, offset)
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "blades": 6,
  "effect": "lens_blur",
  "radius": 10,
  "rotation": 15,
  "roundness": 0.2
}
```

## `unsharp_mask`

Sharpens by adding back a fraction of what a Gaussian blur takes away; coverage is left as it is. (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | float | 50.0 | 0 or more | Percent of the difference added back. |
| `radius` | float | 1.0 | 0 to 100 | Gaussian sigma in pixels of the soft copy; the size of the detail it sharpens. |
| `threshold` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 255 | Differences smaller than this many levels (of 255) are left alone. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 150,
  "effect": "unsharp_mask",
  "radius": 2,
  "threshold": 0
}
```

## `backdrop`

Blurs what has already been composited behind this layer and draws the layer on top (frosted glass). (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `blur` | float | 24.0 | 0 or more | Gaussian sigma in pixels. |
| `quality` | choice | legacy | legacy, exact | `legacy` is the blur films were first made with, kept so they render as they did (above a sigma of 4 a small source gains or loses up to a quarter of its light); `exact` is the kernel blur: the sigma asked for, no light lost, a reach of 4 sigma. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "blur": 24,
  "effect": "backdrop"
}
```

## `radial_blur`

Radial blur from a point: a zoom, or (with `quality: exact`) a spin. (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | float | 0.1 |  | `zoom`: extra zoom at the end of the smear, 0.1 smears 10%. `spin`: degrees the smear turns through. |
| `x` | float | 0.5 |  | Centre across the frame, as a fraction. |
| `y` | float | 0.5 |  | Centre down the frame, as a fraction. |
| `mode` | choice | zoom | zoom, spin | `zoom` smears along each ray from the centre, `spin` along each circle about it. |
| `quality` | choice | legacy | legacy, exact | `legacy` is the blur films were first made with, kept so they render as they did (above a sigma of 4 a small source gains or loses up to a quarter of its light); `exact` is the kernel blur: the sigma asked for, no light lost, a reach of 4 sigma. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by its reach (blur radius, distance, offset)
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 0.1,
  "effect": "radial_blur",
  "x": 0.5,
  "y": 0.5
}
```

## `glow`

Adds a blurred copy back on top, so bright parts bleed light. (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | float | 24.0 | 0 or more | Blur sigma of the halo in pixels. |
| `strength` | float | 1.0 | 0 or more | How much of the halo is added back (1 = as bright as the source). |
| `threshold` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 1 | Only parts brighter than this (0..1 luma) glow; 0 makes everything glow. |
| `color` | color | none |  | Colour of the halo; leave out to glow in the layer's own colours. |
| `quality` | choice | legacy | legacy, exact | `legacy` is the blur films were first made with, kept so they render as they did (above a sigma of 4 a small source gains or loses up to a quarter of its light); `exact` is the kernel blur: the sigma asked for, no light lost, a reach of 4 sigma. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by its reach (blur radius, distance, offset)
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "color": [
    255,
    200,
    120
  ],
  "effect": "glow",
  "radius": 24,
  "strength": 1,
  "threshold": 0
}
```

## `film_halation`

Film halation: the brightest parts ring with a wide red-orange halo, as light scattered back through the film base exposes it again. (effect, platform)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold` | float | 0.6 | 0 to 1 | Light above this (luma, 0..1) halates; in a linear_light film that is light itself. |
| `radius` | float | 40.0 | 0 or more | Gaussian sigma of the halo in pixels. |
| `strength` | float | 0.5 | 0 or more | The luma added back as a fraction of the light that passed the threshold, summed over the picture. |
| `color` | color | [255.0,90.0,40.0,1.0] |  | Hue of the halo; only its hue counts, the strength sets how much light it adds. |
| `quality` | choice | legacy | legacy, exact | `legacy` is the blur films were first made with, kept so they render as they did (above a sigma of 4 a small source gains or loses up to a quarter of its light); `exact` is the kernel blur: the sigma asked for, no light lost, a reach of 4 sigma. |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by its reach (blur radius, distance, offset)
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "color": [
    255,
    90,
    40
  ],
  "effect": "film_halation",
  "radius": 40,
  "strength": 0.5,
  "threshold": 0.6
}
```

## `add_grain`

Film grain as After Effects' Add Grain makes it: seeded, zero-mean, with a size, softness and aspect in px, colour or mono, and a response to shadows, midtones and highlights. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | choice | custom | custom, fine_35mm, coarse_16mm, vintage_8mm | a film look that replaces intensity, size, softness, saturation, shadows and highlights; custom uses the parameters below |
| `intensity` | float | 0.5 | 0 to 10 | standard deviation of the grain where its tone weight is 1, in 4% of full scale (1 = 10.2 levels of 255) |
| `size` | float | 1.5 | 0.5 to 20 | correlation length of the grain in px: the lag at which two grains agree 1/e as much as one agrees with itself |
| `aspect` | float | 1.0 | 0.25 to 4 | width of a grain over its height (above 1 stretches it sideways) |
| `softness` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 8 | extra blur of the grain in px (a Gaussian's standard deviation); the grain stays at the same strength |
| `saturation` | float | 0.3 | 0 to 1 | 0 = one grain for all three channels (mono), 1 = each channel its own; every channel keeps the full strength |
| `shadows` | float | 1.0 | 0 to 2 | grain strength in the darks, a multiple of intensity |
| `midtones` | float | 1.0 | 0 to 2 | grain strength in the midtones |
| `highlights` | float | 1.0 | 0 to 2 | grain strength in the lights |
| `rate` | float | 24.0 | 0 to 60 | grain redraws per second of the layer's time (0 = frozen) |
| `seed` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 100000 | a different seed is a different, equally good pattern |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "effect": "add_grain",
  "preset": "fine_35mm",
  "seed": 3
}
```

## `aura`

Soft mesh-gradient light: up to six coloured points blended into one smooth, band-free field. (generator, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | color | [10.0,12.0,24.0,1.0] |  | ground colour where no point reaches |
| `c1` | color | [91.0,61.0,245.0,1.0] |  | colour of point 1 (alpha 0 turns a point off) |
| `p1` | vec2 | [0.22,0.28] |  | position of point 1, share of the frame (0..1) |
| `c2` | color | [31.0,181.0,224.0,1.0] |  | colour of point 2 |
| `p2` | vec2 | [0.78,0.24] |  | position of point 2 |
| `c3` | color | [255.0,95.0,158.0,1.0] |  | colour of point 3 |
| `p3` | vec2 | [0.7,0.78] |  | position of point 3 |
| `c4` | color | [255.0,179.0,90.0,1.0] |  | colour of point 4 |
| `p4` | vec2 | [0.2,0.82] |  | position of point 4 |
| `c5` | color | [0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0] |  | colour of point 5 (off by default; set alpha above 0) |
| `p5` | vec2 | [0.5,0.5] |  | position of point 5 |
| `c6` | color | [0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0] |  | colour of point 6 (off by default; set alpha above 0) |
| `p6` | vec2 | [0.5,0.5] |  | position of point 6 |
| `softness` | float | 0.46 | 0.05 to 2 | how far each point spreads, share of the frame height |
| `ground` | float | 0.01 | 0 to 0.6 | how much of the ground colour shows far from every point (0 fills the frame with point colours) |
| `drift` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 1 | idle wander of every point, cycles per second (0 holds still) |
| `swirl` | float | 0.06 | 0 to 0.3 | how far a wandering point strays, share of the frame |
| `glow` | float | 0.25 | 0 to 1 | extra brightness where several points overlap |
| `vivid` | float | 0.15 | 0 to 1 | pushes the blend away from grey, so opposite hues stay clean |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "params": {
    "base": "#0a0c18",
    "c1": "#5b3df5",
    "c2": "#1fb5e0",
    "c3": "#ff5f9e",
    "c4": "#ffb35a",
    "c5": "#000000",
    "c6": "#000000",
    "drift": 0.0,
    "glow": 0.25,
    "ground": 0.01,
    "p1": [
      0.22,
      0.28
    ],
    "p2": [
      0.78,
      0.24
    ],
    "p3": [
      0.7,
      0.78
    ],
    "p4": [
      0.2,
      0.82
    ],
    "p5": [
      0.5,
      0.5
    ],
    "p6": [
      0.5,
      0.5
    ],
    "softness": 0.46,
    "swirl": 0.06,
    "vivid": 0.15
  },
  "shader": "aura",
  "type": "texture"
}
```

Blocks stop updating and keep their old pixels, smearing along a drifting vector, like video that lost its keyframes. (effect, shader plugin)

## `displacement_map`

Moves the layer's pixels by the colours of another layer, as After Effects' Displacement Map does. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `horizontal` | choice | red | off, red, green, blue, alpha, luma | the map channel that moves pixels along x (off: none) |
| `vertical` | choice | green | off, red, green, blue, alpha, luma | the map channel that moves pixels along y (off: none) |
| `max_x` | float | 20.0 | -400 to 400 | px a channel at full strength moves pixels right (negative: left); half strength stands still |
| `max_y` | float | 20.0 | -400 to 400 | px a channel at full strength moves pixels down (negative: up) |
| `outside` | choice | pin | pin, wrap | beyond the frame: the edge pixels stretch (pin), or the picture repeats (wrap) |

* input `map`: the picture of another layer, named by id -- the layer whose colours steer the pixels; hide it to use it only as a map
* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand_x=abs(max_x) expand_y=abs(max_y)` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "effect": "displacement_map",
  "horizontal": "luma",
  "map": "ripples",
  "max_x": 30,
  "outside": "wrap",
  "vertical": "off"
}
```

| `shadow` | color | [16.0,16.0,48.0,1.0] |  | colour of the darkest tones |
| `light` | color | [255.0,214.0,160.0,1.0] |  | colour of the lightest tones |
| `amount` | float | 1.0 | 0 to 1 | 0 keeps the original, 1 is fully mapped |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 1.0,
  "effect": "duotone",
  "light": "#ffd6a0",
  "shadow": "#101030"
}
```

## `echo`

A soft fading trail of the layer toward one side: up to 8 faint ghosts that overlap into a smear, not separate hard copies. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | float | 0.55 | 0 to 1 | 0 is the original, 1 is the full trail length and brightness |
| `copies` | float | 5.0 | 2 to 10 | pictures in total, the layer included; the farthest has no weight, so copies - 2 ghosts show (at most 8) |
| `travel` | float | 36.0 | 4 to 120 | px from the layer to the farthest ghost at amount 1 (the farthest sits at travel * amount) |
| `angle` | float | -18.0 | -180 to 180 | direction of the trail in degrees from +x with y down: 0 right, 90 down, -90 up |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand=abs(travel)*amount` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 0.55,
  "angle": -18.0,
  "copies": 5.0,
  "effect": "echo",
  "travel": 36.0
}
```

## `edge_glow`

Finds the edges in the picture and lights them: a blueprint, circuit or neon-outline look. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strength` | float | 1.0 | 0 to 3 | edge brightness |
| `width` | float | 1.5 | 0.5 to 6 | edge thickness in px |
| `tint` | color | [90.0,210.0,255.0,1.0] |  | edge colour |
| `keep` | float | 0.35 | 0 to 1 | how much of the original picture stays |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand=width` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json

  "effect": "edge_glow",

  "strength": 1.0,
  "tint": "#5ad2ff",
  "width": 1.5
}
```

A fading trail: every frame keeps a fraction of what the effect drew one frame earlier. (effect, shader plugin)

| `y` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 1 | origin, share of the height (0 is the top) |

| `tint` | color | [197.0,220.0,255.0,1.0] |  | colour of the light |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 0.0,
  "effect": "lightning",
  "seed": 3.0,
  "tint": "#c5dcff",
  "x": 0.5,
  "y": 0.0
}
```

## `liquid`

Warps the picture like heat over water or a slow melt; good for dream and memory cuts. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | float | 12.0 | 0 to 60 | displacement in px |
| `scale` | float | 0.006 | 0.001 to 0.03 | size of the swirls (smaller is bigger swirls) |
| `speed` | float | 0.4 | 0 to 3 | how fast it moves |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand=amount` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 12.0,
  "effect": "liquid",
  "scale": 0.006,
  "speed": 0.4
}
```

## `mirror`

Reflects one half of the layer onto the other. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | float | 0.5 | 0 to 1 | where the mirror line sits, share of the width |
| `vertical` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 1 | 0 mirrors left/right, 1 mirrors top/bottom |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "axis": 0.5,
  "effect": "mirror",
  "vertical": 0.0
}
```

## `motion_tile`

Repeats the layer as tiles over an output that is larger or smaller than the layer, as After Effects' Motion Tile does. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tile_center` | vec2 | [0.5,0.5] |  | where the middle tile sits, as a share of the layer's width and height (After Effects counts pixels) |
| `tile_width` | float | 100.0 | 1 to 1000 | width of one tile, % of the layer's width; the whole layer is drawn into every tile |
| `tile_height` | float | 100.0 | 1 to 1000 | height of one tile, % of the layer's height |
| `output_width` | float | 100.0 | 1 to 1000 | width of the result, % of the layer's width; past 100 the layer grows, below 100 it is cropped |
| `output_height` | float | 100.0 | 1 to 1000 | height of the result, % of the layer's height |
| `mirror_edges` | choice | off | off, on | on: every other tile is flipped, so neighbouring tiles meet edge to edge |
| `phase` | float | 0.0 | -36000 to 36000 | degrees; each row (or column) is shifted this far further than the one before, 360 being a whole tile |
| `horizontal_phase_shift` | choice | off | off, on | on: the phase shifts rows sideways; off: it shifts columns up and down |
| `gutter_size` | float | 0.0 | 0 to 1000 | px of gap between tiles (not in After Effects) |
| `gutter_color` | color | [0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0] |  | what fills the gaps (not in After Effects) |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand_x=box_w*(output_width-100)/200 expand_y=box_h*(output_height-100)/200` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "effect": "motion_tile",
  "mirror_edges": "on",
  "output_height": 300,
  "output_width": 300,
  "tile_height": 40,
  "tile_width": 40
}
```

## `noise`

Smooth monochrome value noise, drifting over time. Use as a matte, a displacement source or a texture. (generator, shader plugin)

| `speed` | float | 0.3 | 0 to 5 | drift per second |
| `low` | color | [0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0] |  | colour of the low values |
| `high` | color | [255.0,255.0,255.0,1.0] |  | colour of the high values |
| `contrast` | float | 1.0 | 0.2 to 4 | 1 = natural, higher = harder |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): does not reach past the layer's own pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json

  "params": {
    "contrast": 1.0,
    "high": "#ffffff",
    "low": "#000000",
    "scale": 120.0,
    "speed": 0.3
  },
  "shader": "noise",
  "type": "texture"
}
```

## `tilt_shift`

Blurs everything outside a horizontal band so a scene reads as a miniature. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `focus` | float | 0.5 | 0 to 1 | vertical centre of the sharp band (fraction of the height) |
| `band` | float | 0.18 | 0.02 to 0.6 | half-height of the sharp band |
| `blur` | float | 14.0 | 0 to 60 | maximum blur radius in px |
| `quality` | choice | legacy | legacy, exact | `legacy` blurs with 16 spiral taps; `exact` blends between exact Gaussian blurs of sigma blur/6, blur/3 and blur/2, so the blur grows smoothly with the distance from the band and keeps all of its light |

* passes: `soft1` (x1.0), `soft2` (x1.0), `soft3` (x1.0), `main` (x1.0)
* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand=blur*(1+quality)` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in linear numbers

```json
{
  "band": 0.18,
  "blur": 14.0,
  "effect": "tilt_shift",
  "focus": 0.5,
  "quality": "legacy"
}
```

## `turbulent_displace`

Wobbles the layer by a noise layer, like After Effects' Turbulent Displace; drive the noise to animate it. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | float | 24.0 | 0 to 400 | the most a pixel moves, px, in each direction |
| `outside` | choice | pin | pin, wrap | beyond the frame: the edge pixels stretch (pin), or the picture repeats (wrap) |

* input `noise`: the picture of another layer, named by id -- a noise picture, for example a `noise` texture layer (hidden); its brightness is the field
* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand=abs(amount)` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 40,
  "effect": "turbulent_displace",
  "noise": "noise_layer"
}
```

## `vhs`

Worn tape: wobbling lines, colour bleed, tracking noise and a rolling bar. (effect, shader plugin)

| parameter | type | default | range | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | float | 0.5 | 0 to 1 | overall strength |
| `bleed` | float | 6.0 | 0 to 30 | horizontal colour smear in px |
| `noise` | float | 0.25 | 0 to 1 | tracking noise strength |

* layer space (`effect_space: "layer"`): grows the layer's picture by `@bounds expand_x=(29+bleed)*amount expand_y=0` pixels
* colour (`color.linear_light`): computes in display numbers

```json
{
  "amount": 0.5,
  "bleed": 6.0,
  "effect": "vhs",
  "noise": 0.25
}
```
